title: Run list version lists: empty-store fill, catch-up and offline totals
description: Run on an isolated, paired iOS dev client against a gateway with version lists and a fixture of at least 120 live runs, some active, one row of about 2.5 MB. IOS_SIMULATOR and METRO_PORT select its own stack; FARMSLOT_D12_CHECKPOINTS names the controller directory that holds and releases the reconnect, changes runs, stops and restarts the gateway, and cold-restarts the app. The D12 native boot runs the same phases through prove-d12-native.mjs with --trigger=false, and wipes the container before its first launch instead of reset-store.

proofTargets.claim: An empty store fills through one version read and run.list { ids } pages, each within the 60 s request timeout and at most 2 MB except a page carrying one larger row alone, and history then shows every live run with no 80-row limit.
After five runs change, the client reads exactly those ids in pages and no full run list.
A cold start with the gateway stopped shows the whole stored history and its total, and sends no run list read.
Three runs changed while the gateway was down are the only ids read on its new epoch.

reset-store.intent: Relaunch the app with only its resource store deleted.

cold-fill.intent: Open history in the connected app and read the fill until it settles.

assert-cold-fill.intent: Require one version read first, bounded pages and the whole history.

catch-up.intent: Hold the reconnect, change five runs, release it and read the catch-up.

assert-catch-up.intent: Require pages for exactly the changed ids and no full run list read.

offline-totals.intent: Stop the gateway, relaunch the app and read the stored history.

assert-offline-totals.intent: Require the whole stored history and total with no run list reply.

recover-catch-up.intent: Change three runs while the gateway is down and read the new epoch.

assert-recover-catch-up.intent: Require pages on the new epoch for exactly the three changed ids.
